note: v1 95.80 (seeds 0/11 95.80/95.92), first draft of the AMBIENT / HALF-TIME INTERLUDE, 'Underpass': the album's breath between Hairline and Overpass Rain - walking through an underpass at night with the city's drum & bass heard through concrete. A dark wobbly grand and a stretched-voice pad walk from G minor down to F minor (ending on Fm9 for Overpass Rain); the amen plays only in two half-time sections, kick on the one and snare on the three; and where the beat is not, the whole amen is fed silently through wM's granular cloud and a long hall, so the next room's music is smeared into the walls while a low voice drifts. The second half-time adds a glass bell. No roll, no skip, no fracture. (Draft 1 ran the smeared echoes everywhere and measured as one long sameness, 76; giving them only the beatless sections made the shape.) Levels: -13.0 LUFS, true peak -1.0 dBTP, run 2.

v2 97.06 (seeds 0/11 97.06/97.16 vs v1 95.80/95.93): A CLEARER TUNNEL - a mix polish of the interlude. The washed piano and the stretched-voice pad were piling up at 200-470 Hz (+7 dB over the genre) while the half-time kick's body around 100-130 Hz sat 8-10 dB under and the top had no air. The master EQ now moves the weight: the sub's 45 Hz boom -4, the kick's body at 110 Hz +4, cuts at 220 Hz (-3) and 450 Hz (-6) where the tunnel was muddy, and air above 13 kHz (+3) for the glass bell and the walls' grains. Spectrum 84 -> 92; levels unchanged in kind (-13.7 LUFS, true peak -1.0 dBTP, run 1-2).

v3 97.52 (seeds 0/11 97.52/97.53 vs v2 re-scored 97.43/97.47): Underpass's FINAL ROUND, on Harry's Soft Concrete notes and chirper-two's seam. INTO THE RAIN: the last eight bars fade the tunnel out under rising rain, so we walk out of the underpass into Overpass Rain's weather (its intro is rain) - the seam's spectral distance 12.8 -> 8.6 dB on my measure. BASS WITH WEIGHT: the mono sine sub gains wM's phantom harmonics above 100 Hz and a little drive, pumped by the half-time kick. TOOLS WITH A JOB: a master tapestop winds the first half-time's beat down into the drift; the piano goes darker and pumps with the kick; a notch sweeps the voice pad on a five-bar LFO so the stretched voices seem to turn. DARKER: the top eased 2 dB, the glass bell quieter. Levels 100: -12.5 LUFS exactly, true peak -1.15 dBTP, run 1. (A piano band-pass on a 7-bar LFO and heavier harmonics both chopped the half-times into pieces - 11-12 sections - and were dropped.)
